question: When you first changed the closest-hit traversal stack to also store each pushed child's entry distance, how did its A/B against the round-4 binary come out? Give the numbers.
answer:
The entered-distance stack (pushing each deferred child together with the t at which the ray entered it, so a pop needs only the compare `entered <= t_max_q` and touches no memory when pruned) was bit-identical to round 4 on all three scenes, and its interleaved A/B against the round-4 binary came out in its favour:

- 8 paired rounds at 512x512 / 64 spp, seed 1, 12 frames per round
- base (round-4 binary): render_ms_best min = 44.493 ms, mean = 46.042 ms
- candidate (entered-distance stack): min = 44.425 ms, mean = 45.607 ms
- 6 of the 8 paired rounds favoured the candidate (mean gain ≈ 0.44 ms, best-case gain ≈ 0.07 ms)

So it was kept, and it became part of the state snapshotted as `_b/pathtracer`, which is the revert point/A-B base for everything after it. I know this from my own working-memory entry for that experiment (evidence messages 78-88), which recorded the byte-identity check on the three scenes plus those exact min/mean figures and the 6/8 pair count. A follow-up experiment on the same stack — also carrying the child's payload so a pop performs no global load at all — was measured against that entered-only base separately: base 43.875 ms min / 45.583 ms mean vs candidate 43.226 / 44.906, 5/8 pairs, ≈ -0.68 ms mean, and that was kept too.

question: When you first changed the closest-hit traversal stack to also store each pushed child's entry distance, how did its A/B against the round-4 binary come out? Give the numbers.
answer:
The entered-distance stack (each pushed BVH child stored with its entry t, so a pop's box test reduces to `entered <= t_max_q` and pruned pops touch no memory) was a win, and I kept it.

How I measured it: interleaved A/B against the round-4 binary, 8 rounds x 12 frames at 512x512, 64 spp, seed 1, on the default scene, with bit-identity checked on all three scene configs first (PFMs byte-identical to round 4 on default, alt-view and caustic-closeup).

Numbers (render_ms_best per round, aggregated):
- round-4 base: min 44.493 ms, mean 46.042 ms
- entered-distance candidate: min 44.425 ms, mean 45.607 ms
- paired rounds favouring the candidate: 6 of 8

So the gain was small but consistent — about 0.07 ms on the minimum and ~0.44 ms on the paired mean, with the majority of paired rounds going to the candidate. I kept it on that evidence, and it is part of the state later snapshotted as _b (the revert point for the subsequent stack-payload and child-pair experiments). This is recorded in my working memory entry 'round5-glass-and-stack', citing history messages 78-88.

question: When you first changed the closest-hit traversal stack to also store each pushed child's entry distance, how did its A/B against the round-4 binary come out? Give the numbers.
answer:
The entered-distance stack (pushing each deferred child's entry t with it, so a pop only needs `entered <= t_max_q`) beat the round-4 binary in that A/B.

Numbers, from my round-5 log entry for that experiment (8 interleaved rounds x 12 frames, 512x512, 64 spp, seed 1):
- base (round-4 binary): render_ms_best minimum 44.493 ms, mean of per-round bests 46.042 ms
- candidate (entered-distance stack): minimum 44.425 ms, mean 45.607 ms
- 6 of the 8 interleaved pairs favoured the candidate
- it was bit-identical on all three scenes (default, alt-view, caustic-closeup) versus the round-4 reference PFMs

So the win was small but consistent (-0.07 ms at the floor, -0.44 ms on the paired mean, 6/8 pairs), and the reason it is sound is that entered/exited are independent of the current t limits, t_min_q is constant, and t_max_q only ever tightens, so carrying the entry distance prunes pops without changing any hit result — pruned pops then touch no memory at all. I know this from my own working-memory entry 'round5-glass-and-stack' (evidence messages 78-88), which recorded the A/B immediately after it ran; that change is still in the live tree and in the _b snapshot that later experiments are measured against.
